title.narrative: Emergency Health Response: Improving Access to Lifesaving Healthcare for Vulnerable Communities Affected by ElNiño-Induced Floods in Baidoa District.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn line with the Somalia Humanitarian Fund's reserve allocation 7.1, this emergency health response project is aimed at providing essential and inclusive lifesaving health services, strengthen disease surveillance, and respond to acute watery diarrhea (AWD)/cholera outbreaks among the vulnerable communities in Baidoa District. ACF will specifically work through Mursal Health Center, Bayhaw CTC and one mobile team to reach affected populations in Mursal, Banbusal, Waaberi, War xussein IDPs as well as in Berdale, Horseed, and Howlwadag sub-districts. As per the guidance in the Allocation Strategy and the SHF Program and Operational Manual’s guidance, Action Against Hunger has prioritised coordination and intra-complementarities both at the design and implementation phase to maximise health benefits for the affected populations. In identifying the sites to avoid duplication, Action Against Hunger coordinated closely with HIDIG, a sister NGO equally identified for health response in Baidoa under this SHF allocation strategy. Secondly, malaria prevention activities and ORP points have not been budgeted for because they are fully covered under the Global Fund/MoH funding and Caafimaad Plus Consortium FCDO Elnino response respectively. Approximately 19,989 individuals will benefit directly from this project including people living with disability and from minority ethnic clans. Additionally, refresher training will be provided to 20 health workers (8 men and 12 women) and 45 Community Health Workers (CHWs) on BEmONC, IDSR, Cholera case management, protection mainstreaming and harmonized training package for CHWs. Moreover, the six month project will integrate protection, gender-based violence (GBV), and mental health services, ensuring appropriate referrals to the necessary levels of care. Intentional feedback systems including toll free line, client exit interviews and community meetings have been planned to ensure the project remains responsive and maintains centrality of protection. The project will also strengthen the health facility committee and community-level health service provision in the targeted location, involving the active participation of key community stakeholders, including people living with disabilities and ethnic minority groups who are in the catchment area of the CTC. Finally, the project beneficiaries will be linked (as appropriated) with other ACF managed complementary interventions in the same location, including nutrition, water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH), and food security and livelihoods (FSL) programs supported by FCDO Elnino IRF, ECHO, Italian Embassy and Sidalt/pgt
